messages:
Aisha: Quick follow-up from the gateway streaming RFC — I sketched a lightweight 'termination hint' trailer we can add to upstream responses so frontdoor can make better resume/telemetry decisions. Thoughts?

Marc: sketch? drop it here pls.

Aisha: pasted below. The idea: a final trailer that is small/opaque but carries a few fields: `final_offset`, `resume_token`, `side_effects_safe=true|false`, `observability_tags=[k=v,...]`. frontdoor can use `side_effects_safe=false` to avoid hedging/fanouts.

Aisha: ```
trailer: {
  final_offset: 1342,
  resume_token: "rKV-87a2",
  side_effects_safe: false,
  obs_tags: "model=v2,route=short-gen"
}
```

Samir: I like resume_token. Are we sure we want `side_effects_safe` in a trailer? Upstreams often can't assert that.

Aisha: Good point. Proposal: make it advisory. If unset -> treat as unknown (no automatic retries/hedges). Upstreams that know they executed idempotent path can set true.

Liz (sre): Observability: we'll need structured fields so traces can correlate resumed vs original. `resume_token` should map to span tag. Also prefer base64 short tokens, not long JSONs.

Marc: How does this interact with backpressure/early-abort? If frontdoor sees `final_offset` but client already aborted, do we still ship trailer? Upstream might not be able to write it.

Aisha: It's best-effort. We treat trailer presence as a hint. We must not rely on trailer for correctness. Fallback: server-side snapshots (periodic checkpoints) that can be used when trailer missing.

Samir: Snapshots = heavier. We need a memory/time budget. Maybe only enable snapshotting for flows with `resume_enabled=true` in route config.

Liz (sre): +1 for route opt-in. Also add a metric for "resume_failures_due_to_missing_trailer" so we can track effectiveness.

Marc: Edge concern: how do we authenticate resume_token to prevent tampering / cross-tenant resume? It needs a MAC keyed per-tenant or per-route.

Aisha: Agreed — token format: base64(HMAC_SHA256(tenant_id || seq || snapshot_id, key) || seq || snapshot_id). We'll document rotation semantics.

Samir: For streaming clients that expect low-latency, extra MAC verification per resume is fine (it's cheap). But we should keep size tiny.

Liz (sre): Ops runbook suggestion: if resume verification fails, frontdoor should fall back to canonical downgrade (serve non-resumable variant or return a 409-like `cannot_resume`). Log as security event.

Aisha: One more tradeoff: trailers add complexity for HTTP/2 and gRPC proxies vs plain HTTP chunked. Implementation note: in our proxy runtime, add a small 'trailer-collector' stage that buffers only the final 2KB of the stream looking for trailer delimiter — avoids holding the whole response.

Marc: Nice. Can you add a perf microbenchmark? We should measure collector overhead at 99th p50 p95 for heavy flows.

Aisha: Will do. Plan: (1) prototype collector in edge runtime, (2) enable route opt-in, (3) wire resume_token -> trace tag, (4) bake metrics and run perf job. I'll post results next week.

deploy-bot: deployment queued: edge/runtime/collector-prototype -> canary

Samir: Quick nits — add explicit TTL to resume_token so old tokens can't be reused. Also include `resume_reason` enum (client_abort | upstream_abort | network_error) to aid SLO analysis.

Aisha: Good calls. I'll update the trailer sketch and the route config schema. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
